_doc: 독일어 원문은 루트비히 놀이 엮은 『Mozarts Briefe』(잘츠부르크 1865, 공공 영역) 쪽 스캔을 직접 읽어 옮겼고, 판본의 철자(daß, Theil, -iren 등)와 문장부호를 그대로 두었다. 영어는 레이디 월리스의 1866년 번역(공공 영역)을 그대로 따랐다. 한국어는 이 앱이 새로 옮긴 것이다.

messages.de: Wir sind Gott Lob und Dank glücklich zu Waging, Stain, Ferbertshaim und Wasserburg angekommen.
messages.en: God be praised! we reached Waging, Stain, Ferbertshaim, and Wasserburg safely.
messages.ko: 하느님 덕분에 바깅, 슈타인, 페르베르츠하임을 거쳐 바서부르크까지 무사히 왔어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 59 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Wir sind Gott Lob und Dank glücklich zu Waging, Stain, Ferbertshaim und Wasserburg angekommen.
speak.en: God be praised! // we reached Waging, Stain, Ferbertshaim, / and Wasserburg safely.
speak.ko: 하느님 덕분에 바깅, / 슈타인, / 페르베르츠하임을 거쳐 바서부르크까지 무사히 왔어요.

messages.de: Vor Schinn begegneten wir einer Anzahl Kühe, worunter eine merkwürdig war, — denn sie war einseitig, welches wir noch niemals gesehen haben.
messages.en: Near Schinn we met a drove of cows, and one of these very remarkable, for each side was a different color, which we never before saw.
messages.ko: 쉰에 닿기 전에 소 떼를 만났는데, 그중 한 마리가 참 신기했어요. 양쪽 옆구리 색이 서로 달랐거든요. 그런 소는 처음 봤어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 59 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Vor Schinn begegneten wir einer Anzahl Kühe, / worunter eine merkwürdig war, — / denn sie war einseitig, / welches wir noch niemals gesehen haben.
speak.en: Near Schinn we met a drove of cows, / and one of these very remarkable, / for each side was a different color, / which we never before saw.
speak.ko: 쉰에 닿기 전에 소 떼를 만났는데, / 그중 한 마리가 참 신기했어요. // 양쪽 옆구리 색이 서로 달랐거든요. // 그런 소는 처음 봤어요.

messages.de: …uns geht nichts ab als der Papa. Je nun, Gott wills so haben. Es wird noch alles gut gehen.
messages.en: …we want nothing except you, dear papa. Well, this is the will of God; no doubt all will go on right.
messages.ko: …아쉬운 건 아버지 한 분뿐이에요. 뭐, 하느님 뜻이 그런 거겠지요. 다 잘될 거예요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 59 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.en: …we want nothing except you, / dear papa. // Well, / this is the will of God; / no doubt all will go on right.
speak.ko: …아쉬운 건 아버지 한 분뿐이에요. // 뭐, / 하느님 뜻이 그런 거겠지요. // 다 잘될 거예요.

messages.de: Ich gebe mich ganz gut drein. Ich bin der andere Papa, ich geb auf alles acht.
messages.en: Nothing comes amiss to me; I am quite a second papa, and look after everything.
messages.ko: 저는 뭐든 잘 적응하고 있어요. 제가 바로 두 번째 아빠예요. 모든 걸 다 챙기고 있다고요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 59 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.en: Nothing comes amiss to me; / I am quite a second papa, / and look after everything.
speak.ko: 저는 뭐든 잘 적응하고 있어요. // 제가 바로 두 번째 아빠예요. // 모든 걸 다 챙기고 있다고요.

messages.de: Vor einer halben Stunde … klopfte der Hausknecht an und fragte sich um allerlei Sachen an, und ich antwortete ihm mit aller meiner Ernsthaftigkeit, wie ich im Portrait bin.
messages.en: About half an hour ago … the Boots knocked at the door to take my orders about various things, and I gave them to him with the same grave air that I have in my portrait.
messages.ko: 반 시간 전에 … 여관 일꾼이 문을 두드리고 이것저것 물었어요. 저는 초상화 속 제 모습처럼 아주 근엄하게 대답해 줬지요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 59 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

note.ko: 1777년 9월 23일, 볼프강은 대주교의 궁정을 떠나 어머니와 함께 일자리를 찾아 길을 나섰어요. 아버지는 잘츠부르크에 남았지요. 이 편지는 바로 그날 밤 바서부르크의 여관 ‘슈테른’에서, 어머니가 벌써 반쯤 잠든 사이에 쓴 첫 여행 편지예요. 그가 농담처럼 말한 ‘초상화’는 아마 1777년에 그린, 황금 박차 훈장을 단 초상화일 거예요.
note.en: On 23 September 1777 Wolfgang, released from the Archbishop's service, set out with his mother to look for a post; his father stayed in Salzburg. This is his first letter from the road, written that night at the Stern inn in Wasserburg while his mother was already half asleep. The 'portrait' he jokes about is probably the one painted in 1777 showing him with the papal Order of the Golden Spur.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 59 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

reply.de: Gute Reise, mein Sohn, gib acht!
reply.en: Safe travels, my son, take care!
reply._note: 아버지의 답장 (이 앱이 쓴 짧은 문장, 별자리 잇기용)

text.en: First night of the journey: the Stern inn, Wasserburg

messages.de: Er sagt oft: Wenn ich nicht selbst ein so passionirter Liebhaber der Musik wäre … so hätte ich gewiß schon längst die Geduld bei meiner Arbeit verloren; allein ich bin halt ein Liebhaber von Instrumenten die den Spieler nicht ansetzen und die dauerhaft sind.
messages.en: He often says, "If I were not such a passionate lover of music … I should long ago have lost patience with my work, but I like my instruments to respond to the player, and to be durable."
messages.ko: 그분은 자주 이렇게 말해요. “내가 음악을 이토록 사랑하지 않았다면 … 벌써 오래전에 이 일에 지쳐 버렸을 거요. 하지만 나는 연주자를 저버리지 않고 오래가는 악기가 좋소.”
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 67 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: …so stellt er ihn in die Luft, Regen, Schnee, Sonnenhitze und allen Teufel, damit er zerspringt, und dann legt er Späne ein und leimt sie hinein, damit er recht stark und fest wird.
messages.en: …he exposes it in the air to rain, snow, sun, and every kind of devilry, that it may give way, and then inserts slips of wood which he glues in, making it quite strong and solid.
messages.ko: …공명판을 바깥에 내놓고 비, 눈, 뙤약볕, 온갖 고약한 날씨를 다 맞혀 갈라지게 해요. 그런 다음 나뭇조각을 끼워 아교로 붙여서 아주 튼튼하게 만들어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 67 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Er ist völlig froh wenn er springt; man ist halt hernach versichert, daß ihm nichts mehr geschieht.
messages.en: He is very glad when it does crack, for then he is pretty sure nothing further can happen to it.
messages.ko: 판이 갈라지면 오히려 무척 기뻐해요. 그러고 나면 더는 아무 탈이 없을 거라고 안심할 수 있으니까요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 67 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Ich habe hier und in München schon alle meine 6 Sonaten recht oft auswendig gespielt; … die letzte aus D kommt auf den Pianofortes von Stein unvergleichlich heraus.
messages.en: I have played my six sonatas by heart repeatedly, both here and in Munich. … the last in D, which has an incomparable effect on Stein's pianos.
messages.ko: 여기서도 뮌헨에서도 제 소나타 여섯 곡을 모두 여러 번 외워서 쳤어요. … 마지막 D장조 소나타는 슈타인의 피아노포르테에서 비할 데 없이 잘 울려요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 67 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: „Das hat alles nichts zu bedeuten; die Orgel ist doch in meinen Augen und Ohren der König aller Instrumente.“
messages.en: "That does not signify; the organ always was, both in my eyes and ears, the king of all instruments."
messages.ko: “그런 건 아무 상관 없어요. 제 눈과 귀에 오르간은 언제나 모든 악기의 왕이에요.”
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 67 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

note.ko: 아우크스부르크의 요한 안드레아스 슈타인은 오르간과 피아노포르테를 만든 제작자예요. 볼프강은 슈타인의 악기가 왜 오래가는지 아버지께 설명해요. 공명판을 먼저 날씨에 갈라지게 한 뒤 고쳐 쓰는 거지요. 외워서 쳤다는 소나타 여섯 곡은 피아노 소나타 K. 279–284이고, ‘마지막 D장조’는 K. 284예요.
note.en: Johann Andreas Stein of Augsburg built organs and the fortepianos Mozart praises here. Wolfgang explains to his father why Stein's instruments last: the soundboard is left to crack in the weather first, then mended. The six sonatas he played by heart are his piano sonatas K. 279–284; the 'last in D' is K. 284.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 67 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

reply.de: Schreib mir bald von den Orgeln!
reply.en: Write to me soon about the organs!

messages.de: Ich habe ihm ein Präsent mit dem Hautbois-Concert gemacht; es wird im Zimmer bei Cannabich abgeschrieben. Der Mensch ist närrisch vor Freude …
messages.en: I made him a present of a concerto for the hautboy; it is being copied in Cannabich's room. The man is wild with delight.
messages.ko: 그 사람한테 오보에 협주곡을 선물했어요. 지금 칸나비히 씨 방에서 악보를 베끼고 있어요. 그 사람, 기뻐서 어쩔 줄을 몰라요 …

messages.de: „Ich bin schon vor 15 Jahren hier gewesen; … aber nun bin ich älter und grösser geworden, und so auch in der Musik.“
messages.en: "I was here fifteen years ago, … but now I am older and more advanced, and I may say in music also."
messages.ko: “15년 전에 여기 온 적이 있어요. … 하지만 이제는 나이도 먹고 키도 컸고, 음악도 그만큼 자랐지요.”
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 71 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Das Orchester ist sehr gut und stark; auf jeder Seite 10 bis 11 Violinen, 4 Bratschen, 2 Oboen, 2 Flauti und 2 Clarinetti …
messages.en: The orchestra is very good and numerous. On each side ten or eleven violins, four tenors, two hautboys, two flutes, and two clarionets …

messages.de: Der zweite ist bei der Orgel wie das Kind beim Dreck; man sieht ihm seine Kunst schon im Gesichte an.
messages.en: The second at the organ is like a child trying to lift a millstone. You can see his anguish in his face.
messages.ko: 두 번째 오르가니스트는 오르간 앞에서 흙장난하는 아이 같아요. 그 솜씨가 벌써 얼굴에 다 쓰여 있어요.

messages.de: Morgen muß ich nach dem Hochamt zu der gestrengen Frau Churfürstin, sie will mir absolument Filée stricken lehren …
messages.en: I must go to-morrow after high mass to the illustrious Electress; she is resolved absolument to teach me to knit filee.
messages.ko: 내일은 대미사가 끝나면 지엄하신 선제후비께 가야 해요. 저한테 기어코 필레 뜨개질을 가르치시겠대요 …

speak.de: Morgen muß ich nach dem Hochamt zu der gestrengen Frau Churfürstin, / sie will mir absolument Filée stricken lehren …
speak.en: I must go to-morrow after high mass to the illustrious Electress; / she is resolved absolument to teach me to knit filee.
speak.ko: 내일은 대미사가 끝나면 지엄하신 선제후비께 가야 해요. // 저한테 기어코 필레 뜨개질을 가르치시겠대요 …

note.ko: 만하임은 팔츠 선제후 카를 테오도어의 궁정이 있던 곳이에요. 볼프강은 오케스트라를 이끄는 크리스티안 칸나비히, 오보에 주자 프리드리히 람과 금세 친해졌어요. 람에게 준 협주곡은 오보에 협주곡 C장조 K. 314예요. 그는 15년 전, 일곱 살 때 가족 연주 여행으로 이곳에 온 적이 있어요.
note.en: Mannheim was the seat of the Elector Palatine Carl Theodor. Wolfgang quickly made friends with the orchestra's leader Christian Cannabich and the oboist Friedrich Ramm; the concerto he gave Ramm is the Oboe Concerto in C, K. 314. He had been in Mannheim fifteen years before, aged seven, on the family's concert tour.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 71 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

reply.de: Bravo für das Hautbois-Concert, mein Sohn!
reply.en: Bravo for the oboe concerto, my son!

messages.de: Ich habe heute Vormittag bei Hrn. Cannabich das Rondo zur Sonate für seine Mademoiselle Tochter geschrieben, folglich haben sie mich nicht mehr weggelassen.
messages.en: This forenoon, at Herr Cannabich's, I wrote the Rondo of the sonata for his daughter; so they would not let me leave them all day.
messages.ko: 오늘 오전에 칸나비히 씨 댁에서 그 집 따님을 위한 소나타의 론도를 썼어요. 그랬더니 다들 저를 하루 종일 놓아주질 않았어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 73 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Ich habe heute Vormittag bei Hrn. Cannabich das Rondo zur Sonate für seine Mademoiselle Tochter geschrieben, / folglich haben sie mich nicht mehr weggelassen.
speak.en: This forenoon, / at Herr Cannabich's, / I wrote the Rondo of the sonata for his daughter; / so they would not let me leave them all day.
speak.ko: 오늘 오전에 칸나비히 씨 댁에서 그 집 따님을 위한 소나타의 론도를 썼어요. // 그랬더니 다들 저를 하루 종일 놓아주질 않았어요.

messages.de: „Es ist jetzt, glaube ich, 15 Jahr, daß Er nicht hier war.“ — „Ja, Euer Durchlaucht, 15 Jahr, daß ich nicht die Gnade gehabt habe.“ — „Er spielt unvergleichlich.“
messages.en: "I think it is now fifteen years since you were here?" "Yes, your Highness, it is fifteen years since I had that honor." "You play inimitably."
messages.ko: “그대가 여기 온 지 15년쯤 되었지?” — “예, 전하. 그 영광을 누린 지 15년이 되었습니다.” — “그대의 연주는 비할 데가 없구나.”
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 73 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Ich kann nicht poetisch schreiben; ich bin kein Dichter. Ich kann die Redensarten nicht so künstlich eintheilen, daß sie Schatten und Licht geben; ich bin kein Maler.
messages.en: I cannot write poetically, for I am no poet. I cannot make fine artistic phrases that cast light and shadow, for I am no painter.
messages.ko: 저는 시처럼 쓸 줄 몰라요. 시인이 아니니까요. 말을 솜씨 있게 나눠 빛과 그림자를 드리울 줄도 몰라요. 화가가 아니니까요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 73 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Ich kann sogar durchs Deuten und durch Pantomime meine Gesinnungen und Gedanken nicht ausdrücken; ich bin kein Tänzer. Ich kann es aber durch Töne; ich bin ein Musikus.
messages.en: I can neither by signs nor by pantomime express my thoughts and feelings, for I am no dancer; but I can by tones, for I am a musician.
messages.ko: 몸짓이나 무언극으로 제 마음과 생각을 나타낼 줄도 몰라요. 무용수가 아니니까요. 하지만 소리로는 할 수 있어요. 저는 음악가니까요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 73 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Ich wünsche Ihnen, daß Sie so viele Jahre leben möchten, als man Jahre braucht, um gar nichts Neues mehr in der Musik machen zu können.
messages.en: I wish that you may live as many years as must elapse before no more new music can be composed.
messages.ko: 음악에서 더는 새로운 걸 하나도 만들 수 없게 될 때까지 걸리는 햇수만큼, 아버지가 오래오래 사시기를 빌어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 73 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

note.ko: 레오폴트 모차르트의 생일은 11월 14일, 영명축일(성 레오폴트 축일)은 11월 15일이라 볼프강은 두 날을 함께 축하해요. 칸나비히의 딸 로자에게 써 준 소나타는 피아노 소나타 C장조 K. 309예요. 이 편지를 쓰기 전에 그는 선제후 카를 테오도어와 궁정 앞에서 연주했어요.
note.en: Leopold Mozart's birthday fell on 14 November and his name-day, St Leopold's, on 15 November, so Wolfgang sends a double greeting. The sonata for Cannabich's daughter Rosa is the Piano Sonata in C, K. 309. Shortly before, he had played for the Elector Carl Theodor and his court.

messages.de: Hier ist es dermalen nichts mit dem Churfürsten. Ich war vorgestern in der Academie bei Hof um eine Antwort zu bekommen.
messages.en: All is at an end, for the present, with the Elector. I went to the court concert the day before yesterday, in the hope of getting an answer.
messages.ko: 선제후 일은 당분간 끝났어요. 그저께 답을 들으려고 궁정 음악회에 갔었어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 83 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: „Nu, da ist Einer, der das gewöhnliche schöne Schicksal vom Hof hat.“
messages.en: "I bring you a man who shares the usual happy fate of those who have to do with courts."
messages.ko: “자, 여기 궁정이 흔히 내려 주는 그 멋진 운명을 맞은 사람이 왔소.”

messages.de: Sie spielte darauf ganz serieuse meine Sonate. Hören Sie, ich konnte mich des Weinens nicht enthalten. Endlich kamen auch der Mutter, Tochter und dem Hrn. Schatzmeister die Thränen in die Augen …
messages.en: She then played my sonata, but looked very grave. Do you know, I really could not suppress my tears; and at last they had all tears in their eyes—mother, daughter, and Schatzmeister …
messages.ko: 그러고 나서 로자가 아주 진지하게 제 소나타를 쳤어요. 글쎄, 저는 눈물을 참을 수가 없었어요. 결국 어머니도, 딸도, 재무관 어른도 눈시울이 젖었어요 …
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 83 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.en: She then played my sonata, / but looked very grave. // Do you know, / I really could not suppress my tears; / and at last they had all tears in their eyes—mother, / daughter, / and Schatzmeister …

messages.de: Bedenken Sie nur diese allzu gewisse Wahrheit, daß sich nicht alles thun läßt, was man im Sinne hat.
messages.en: Reflect also on this most undoubted truth, that we cannot do all we wish.
messages.ko: 이 너무도 확실한 진실을 생각해 보세요. 마음먹은 걸 다 할 수는 없다는 것 말이에요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 83 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.en: Reflect also on this most undoubted truth, / that we cannot do all we wish.
speak.ko: 이 너무도 확실한 진실을 생각해 보세요. // 마음먹은 걸 다 할 수는 없다는 것 말이에요.

messages.de: Kurz und gut aber! Nur nicht kriechen! Denn das kann ich nicht leiden.
messages.en: But short and to the point—no cringing! for that I cannot bear.
messages.ko: 다만 짧고 분명하게요! 굽실거리지는 말고요! 그건 제가 못 견뎌요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 83 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Kurz und gut aber! // Nur nicht kriechen! // Denn das kann ich nicht leiden.
speak.en: But short and to the point—no cringing! // for that I cannot bear.
speak.ko: 다만 짧고 분명하게요! // 굽실거리지는 말고요! // 그건 제가 못 견뎌요.

note.ko: 몇 주를 기다린 끝에 볼프강은 선제후가 자리를 주지 않는다는 답을 들었어요. 친구들은 곧바로 그를 만하임에 붙잡아 두려 했어요. 플루트 주자 벤틀링은 네덜란드인 애호가(‘우리 인도 사람’)가 플루트 협주곡과 사중주를 주문한다는 소식을 전했지요. 놀의 판본에는 사례금이 200플로린으로, 월리스의 영어판에는 20플로린으로 적혀 있어요.
note.en: After weeks of waiting, Wolfgang learned that the Elector would not give him a post. His friends at once tried to keep him in Mannheim: the flautist Wendling brought an offer from a Dutch amateur ('our Indian') for flute concertos and quartets. Nohl prints the fee as 200 florins; Wallace's English has 'twenty'.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 83 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

reply.de: Gott hat es so gewollt, mein Sohn.
reply.en: God willed it so, my son.

messages.de: Das erste ist, daß ich Ihnen schreibe, wie es mir und meinen werthen Freunden in Kirchheim-Boland ergangen ist. Es war eine Vacanzreise und weiter nichts.
messages.en: The first thing I mean to write about is how my worthy friends and I got on at Kirchheim-Boland. It was simply a holiday excursion, and nothing more.
messages.ko: 먼저 제가 소중한 친구들과 키르히하임볼란덴에서 어떻게 지냈는지 써 드릴게요. 그냥 휴가 여행이었지, 그 이상은 아니었어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 91 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.en: Only think of her playing my difficult sonatas at sight, slowly, but without missing a single note.
messages.ko: 생각해 보세요, 그 아가씨가 제 어려운 소나타들을 처음 보자마자, 천천히지만 음 하나 틀리지 않고 쳤어요.

messages.en: I give you my honor I would rather hear my sonatas played by her than by Vogler.
messages.ko: 맹세코, 제 소나타는 포글러보다 그 아가씨가 치는 걸 듣고 싶어요.

messages.de: Ich habe diese bedrückte Familie so lieb, daß ich nichts mehr wünsche, als daß ich sie glücklich machen könnte, und vielleicht kann ich es auch.
messages.en: I am so attached to this oppressed family that my greatest wish is to make them happy, and perhaps I may be able to do so.
messages.ko: 저는 형편이 어려운 이 가족이 너무 좋아서, 그들을 행복하게 해 줄 수 있기만을 바라요. 어쩌면 정말 그럴 수 있을지도 몰라요.

speak.en: You know my greatest desire is—to write operas.
speak.ko: 아시잖아요, / 제 가장 큰 바람은 — / 오페라를 쓰는 거예요.

note.ko: 볼프강은 베버 가족과 함께 키르히하임볼란덴의 궁정으로 연주 여행을 다녀왔어요. 그가 칭찬하는 가수 알로이지아 베버는 악보 필사가이자 프롬프터였던 베버의 둘째 딸이에요. 그 동생 콘스탄체가 훗날 모차르트의 아내가 되지요. 베버 가족을 데리고 이탈리아로 가겠다는 이 계획에 아버지는 크게 놀랐어요.
note.en: Wolfgang had just made a concert trip with the Weber family to the princely court at Kirchheimbolanden. The singer he praises, Aloysia Weber, was the second daughter of the music copyist and prompter Fridolin Weber; her younger sister Constanze would later become Mozart's wife. His plan to take the Webers to Italy alarmed his father.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 91 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: „Nach Gott kommt gleich der Papa!“ das war als Kind mein Wahlspruch oder Axioma und bey dem bleib ich auch noch.
messages.en: "Next to God comes papa" was my axiom when a child, and I still think the same.
messages.ko: “하느님 다음은 바로 아빠!” 어릴 때 제 좌우명이었는데, 지금도 변함없어요.

messages.de: Ich wollte nur wünschen daß Sie meine neue Arie, von welcher ich Ihnen neulich gemeldet habe, von ihr singen hörten, … denn sie ist ganz für sie gemacht …
messages.en: I only wish that you could hear her sing my new aria which I lately mentioned to you, … because it seems made expressly for her …
messages.ko: 얼마 전에 말씀드린 제 새 아리아를 그 아가씨가 부르는 걸 아버지가 들어 보시면 좋겠어요. … 그 곡은 온전히 그 아가씨를 위해 만든 거니까요 …
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 98 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Ich wollte nur wünschen daß Sie meine neue Arie, / von welcher ich Ihnen neulich gemeldet habe, / von ihr singen hörten, / … // denn sie ist ganz für sie gemacht …
speak.en: I only wish that you could hear her sing my new aria which I lately mentioned to you, / … // because it seems made expressly for her …
speak.ko: 얼마 전에 말씀드린 제 새 아리아를 그 아가씨가 부르는 걸 아버지가 들어 보시면 좋겠어요. // … // 그 곡은 온전히 그 아가씨를 위해 만든 거니까요 …

messages.de: Nun muß ich Ihnen aber sagen, daß ich so erschrocken war und mir die Thränen in die Augen kamen, als ich in Ihrem letzten Brief las, daß Sie so schlecht gekleidet daher gehen müssen.
messages.en: I must now tell you I was so shocked that tears came to my eyes, on reading in your last letter that you are obliged to go about so shabbily dressed.
messages.ko: 그런데 꼭 말씀드려야겠어요. 지난 편지에서 아버지가 그렇게 초라한 옷차림으로 다니셔야 한다는 걸 읽고, 너무 놀라서 눈물이 났어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 98 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

messages.de: Mein allerliebster Papa! meine Schuld ist das gewiß nicht — das wissen Sie.
messages.en: My very dearest papa, this is certainly not my fault; you know it is not.
messages.ko: 사랑하는 아빠! 그건 정말 제 탓이 아니에요. 아버지도 아시잖아요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 98 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Mein allerliebster Papa! // meine Schuld ist das gewiß nicht — / das wissen Sie.
speak.en: My very dearest papa, / this is certainly not my fault; / you know it is not.
speak.ko: 사랑하는 아빠! // 그건 정말 제 탓이 아니에요. // 아버지도 아시잖아요.

messages.de: Ich habe nun meine ganze Hoffnung nach Paris, denn die deutschen Fürsten sind alle Knicker. Ich werde nach allen meinen Kräften arbeiten um bald das Vergnügen zu haben Ihnen aus den dermaligen betrübten Umständen herauszuhelfen.
messages.en: My whole hopes are now centred in Paris, for German princes are all niggards. I mean to work with all my strength, that I may soon have the happiness of extricating you from your present distressing circumstances.
messages.ko: 이제 제 희망은 모두 파리에 걸려 있어요. 독일의 군주들은 다 구두쇠니까요. 온 힘을 다해 일해서, 하루빨리 아버지를 지금의 딱한 형편에서 건져 드리는 기쁨을 누리고 싶어요.
messages.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 98 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

speak.de: Ich habe nun meine ganze Hoffnung nach Paris, / denn die deutschen Fürsten sind alle Knicker. // Ich werde nach allen meinen Kräften arbeiten um bald das Vergnügen zu haben Ihnen aus den dermaligen betrübten Umständen herauszuhelfen.
speak.en: My whole hopes are now centred in Paris, / for German princes are all niggards. // I mean to work with all my strength, / that I may soon have the happiness of extricating you from your present distressing circumstances.
speak.ko: 이제 제 희망은 모두 파리에 걸려 있어요. // 독일의 군주들은 다 구두쇠니까요. // 온 힘을 다해 일해서, / 하루빨리 아버지를 지금의 딱한 형편에서 건져 드리는 기쁨을 누리고 싶어요.

note.ko: 만하임을 떠나기 일주일쯤 전의 편지예요. 아버지는 여행 경비 때문에 빚을 지고 옷차림까지 초라해졌다고 써 보냈고, 볼프강은 그 소식에 눈물을 흘렸어요. 새 아리아는 알로이지아 베버를 위해 쓴 〈논 소 돈데 비에네〉 K. 294예요. 1778년 3월 14일, 그는 어머니와 함께 파리로 떠났어요.
note.en: Written a week before leaving Mannheim. Leopold had written that the journey's costs left him going about shabbily dressed, and Wolfgang was moved to tears. The new aria is 'Non so d'onde viene', K. 294, written for Aloysia Weber. On 14 March 1778 he set out with his mother for Paris.
note.source: Mozarts Briefe (L. Nohl, 1865), Nr. 98 · public domain · https://archive.org/details/mozartsbriefehe00mozagoog

reply.de: Gott segne dich in Paris, mein Sohn.
reply.en: God bless you in Paris, my son.
